title: Standard method for microCT-based additive manufacturing quality control 3: Surface roughness
author: Plessis, Sperling, et al.

steps.title: Build sample via selective laser melting
steps.instruction: Use the custom SLM platform inside a commercial LENS enclosure; employ an IPG YLS 5000 ytterbium 5 kW fibre laser (1076 nm wavelength, 50 µm core) with an Intelliweld 30 FC V scanner; feed gas‑atomized Ti6Al4V powder (20‑60 µm) from TLS Technik GmbH onto a Ti6Al4V base plate (150 mm diameter, ~40 mm thick); set hatch parameters to 3 kW power, 3 m·s⁻¹ speed, 240 µm spot size; for contour scans use 1 kW laser power while varying hatch‑contour distance and speed as required; fabricate the single test sample described in Table 1.

steps.title: Measure surface with tactile probe
steps.instruction: Prepare a 10 × 10 × 10 mm coupon; at the National Metrology Institute of South Africa, use a Taylor Hobson tactile probe (2 µm radius) to acquire points spaced 3 µm along the scan direction, collecting 1000 points per line; space each line 1 µm apart and record 3000 lines, covering a 3 × 3 mm area.

steps.title: Acquire microCT scan of sample
steps.instruction: Set the laboratory microCT to 200 kV, 70 µA with a 0.5 mm beam filter; capture images with 500 ms exposure at 2400 equally spaced rotation steps over 360°, yielding a 15 µm voxel size; at each step discard the first image and average the next two; total acquisition time is just under 1 hour, and including warm‑up, background correction and reconstruction the whole process fits within ~2 hours.

steps.title: Reconstruct microCT dataset
steps.instruction: Reconstruct the acquired projections using a strong beam‑hardening correction factor and do not apply any image de‑noising.

steps.title: Process dataset in VGStudioMax
steps.instruction: Open the reconstruction in Volume Graphics VGStudioMax 3.1; apply a basic surface determination and create a region of interest (ROI) from that surface; use the region‑growing tool with high tolerance and the option “avoid other visible ROIs” to select exterior air up to the part edge; invert the selection to obtain the whole part (including pores); run an advanced surface determination using the ROI as the starting contour to obtain a sub‑voxel‑precise exterior surface.

steps.title: Create surface roughness map
steps.instruction: Within the processed dataset, define a 3 mm × 3 mm × 3 mm ROI on the surface and colour it for visibility; generate a best‑fit plane geometry element by selecting approximately 15 points along each edge of the square ROI; right‑click the plane and choose Create → Mesh from geometry element(s); compute a nominal‑actual deviation between this mesh and the actual surface inside the ROI by right‑clicking the ROI and selecting Create → Nominal/actual comparison; the resulting colour map and the accompanying deviation and cumulative histograms provide the surface topography.

steps.title: Export deviation data and calculate Sa
steps.instruction: Export the nominal‑actual comparison to a CSV file containing two columns: deviation value (negative to positive) and corresponding surface‑area contribution; calculate Sa by taking the absolute value of each deviation, multiplying by its surface‑area contribution, summing all products and dividing by the total surface area; optionally obtain Ra by down‑scaling the data or performing a line‑fit on the deviation profile.
